description: Save a new login. Without `password` or `password_file` a strong one is generated here and stored; nothing returns it, so call get_password when you type it into the signup form. Create the login BEFORE submitting a signup, so the password is never lost. Filed into the account's own vault, outside any collection unless `collection` names another.

collection.description: A collection name from health. Default: the account's own vault, outside any collection.

length.description: Length of a generated password. Default 24.

notes.description: Free text kept with the login: recovery codes, security answers, what the account is for.

password.description: A password the account already has, exactly as you were given it. Leave it out to have a strong one generated here; a secret that is already in a file goes as password_file instead, so it is never retyped.

password_file.description: A password the account already has, from a file holding just it (one line; a final line ending is dropped): a downloaded key or a generated credential, which is safer read than retyped. Delete the file once the login is saved. Never type or paste a file's base64 yourself: a retyped file can arrive changed. Give the path of a file in your workspace folders (the roots this client shares; without them /tmp/churn-8rxs9k8t), or have a script that read the file send content_base64 with its sha256.

content_base64.description: The bytes as standard base64, only as a script that read the file wrote them, never typed. Needs sha256.

path.description: A path: a file in your workspace folders (the roots this client shares with the server; without them /tmp/churn-8rxs9k8t); a bare name is taken from the first. Links are refused.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the source file, as sha256sum prints it. Required with content_base64, checked with path.

symbols.description: Whether a generated password contains symbols (!@#$%^&*-_=+). Default true; turn off for sites that refuse them.

totp_secret.description: The site's authenticator key: the base32 secret shown under the 2FA QR code, or the otpauth://totp/ URI it encodes. Store it BEFORE confirming 2FA on the site, then confirm with the code this call returns: the site accepting it proves the key was stored exactly.

url.description: The site's URL, e.g. https://github.com/login; its host is what find_logins' url matches.

username.description: The login name or email the site knows the account by.

name: create_login
title: Create login
